item.title: SNAP showdown: US judges order USDA to use emergency funds for food stamps; Trump seeks court clarification
item.description: President Trump has directed lawyers to seek court clarification on legally funding SNAP benefits amid a government shutdown. Federal judges in Massachusetts and Rhode Island ordered the use of emergency funds to cover food stamp payments, rejecting the USDA's stance. Trump aims to ensure Americans don't go hungry due to the shutdown.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Danger has been averted’: Berlin airport briefly halts flights after unidentified drone sightings
item.description: Berlin Brandenburg Airport experienced flight suspensions for nearly two hours due to unidentified drone sightings, a recurring issue across Europe. Take-offs and landings were halted, leading to flight diversions, as police investigated the drone incursions. This incident highlights a growing "hybrid threat" concern for Germany and other European nations.

item.title: FBI stops ‘ISIS-style’ Halloween attack in Michigan after decoding eerie ‘pumpkin day’ reference
item.description: The FBI thwarted a potential ISIS-inspired attack in Michigan just before Halloween, arresting multiple suspects who allegedly planned a "pumpkin day" assault. Months of online surveillance and an undercover operative led to the arrests, preventing a violent attack over the holiday weekend.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Adin Ross Halloween stream goes viral after he removes contestant who mocked George Floyd’s death live
item.description: Streamer Adin Ross removed a contestant from his Halloween contest for reenacting George Floyd's death. Another contestant appeared as Adolf Hitler, prompting Ross to express shock. These incidents have sparked online debate about Ross's content. Separately, Ross and Drake face a lawsuit in Missouri for allegedly promoting illegal gambling to young people.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Asmongold’s viral rant about America being “White people’s land” turns into major race debate online
item.description: Popular streamer Asmongold ignited a fierce online debate by stating America is "White people's land" and was "fought over." His comments, made while reacting to HasanAbi's remarks about White people in Japan, drew accusations of racism and historical revisionism. Supporters argued he was merely describing how nations are formed through conflict, sparking a significant online clash.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Brazilian police accused of hanging teen gangster’s head ‘like a trophy’ in anti-drug raid that killed over 120
item.description: A brutal police raid in Rio de Janeiro targeting the Red Command drug gang resulted in over 120 deaths, with shocking claims of a decapitated teenager displayed as a trophy. Authorities described the operation as the country's deadliest anti-gang effort, amidst chaos and gun battles. UN officials expressed alarm and called for swift investigations into the horrifying violence.

item.title: UAE Milestone: Abu Dhabi becomes 5th smartest city in the World
item.description: Abu Dhabi has surged to 5th globally in the 2025 IMD Smart City Index, a testament to its strategy linking policy, tech, and visible projects. Residents praise its safety, efficient public transport, and digital services like the TAMM platform. The city's focus on human-centered technology, from autonomous vehicles to AI cleaning fleets, significantly enhances urban living.

item.title: ‘Babies are starving!’: Kamala Harris explodes over Donald Trump’s $300 million ballroom — watch
item.description: Kamala Harris fiercely criticized Donald Trump's plan for a new $300 million White House ballroom, deeming it a luxury project while millions face food aid loss due to the government shutdown. She accused Trump of prioritizing image and excess over the needs of struggling families and children.

item.title: 'Severe water shortages': Pakistan faces 'acute risk' after India’s IWT suspension - report
item.description: Pakistan faces a severe water crisis after India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty, potentially controlling crucial river flows. A recent report highlights Pakistan's limited storage capacity, making it vulnerable to disruptions. India's recent dam operations on the Chenab River, without prior notification, caused downstream drying and sediment release, impacting Pakistan's agriculture, which heavily relies on these waters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Is that Robin Scherbatsky?’: Viral clips on YouTube show 'How I Met Your Mother' star in powerful ex-Marine role
item.description: A viral clip from 'Stumptown' showcases Cobie Smulders, famed as Robin from 'How I Met Your Mother,' in a gripping action role. Her portrayal of ex-Marine Dex Parios rescuing her brother, a young man with Down syndrome, has captivated audiences.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: Zelenskyy says 1.7 lakh Russian troops in Donetsk as fight for Pokrovsk intensifies
item.description: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy reported approximately 170,000 Russian troops are in Donetsk, intensifying efforts to capture Pokrovsk, though he denied the city is fully surrounded. Meanwhile, Ukraine continues long-range strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, with officials warning of rising civilian casualties and a decline in humanitarian funding.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What’s happening in Sudan? UN warns of grave humanitarian crisis following El Fasher’s fall
item.description: El Fasher, North Darfur, has become the epicenter of a humanitarian disaster following its takeover by the RSF after an 18-month siege. The conflict, which began in April 2023 between former allies SAF and RSF, has resulted in mass killings, widespread starvation, and mass displacement, with credible reports of executions and ethnic violence.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Disgusting': JD Vance shuts down 'Hinduphobia' allegations, says he knows Usha has no plans to convert to Christianity but...
item.description: Vice President JD Vance addressed social media speculation regarding his interfaith marriage, clarifying that his wife Usha, a Hindu, has no plans to convert to Christianity. Vance stated that Usha encouraged his re-engagement with his faith and expressed his hope that she might one day share his beliefs, emphasizing his continued love and support for her.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: JD Vance walks into religious fire after hoping his wife Usha will embrace Christianity
item.description: US Vice-President JD Vance sparked controversy by expressing hope his Hindu wife would adopt his Christian faith, despite acknowledging her free will. His remarks at a conservative event drew both applause and backlash, with critics labeling them as Hinduphobic pandering. Vance defended his stance, emphasising Christian beliefs and the desire to share them.
item.dc:creator: Chidanand Rajghatta

item.title: Dubai private school fees 2025–26: What parents should know about ‘Outstanding’ schools
item.description: Dubai's education regulator has set a fee cap for private schools for the 2025-2026 academic year. Tuition increases will be limited to 2.35% for all schools, regardless of their inspection rating. This move aims to ensure affordability for families while maintaining high educational standards. Parents can compare school fees transparently using new tools provided by the regulator.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Hope of every Christian': Indian-origin MAGA activist supports JD Vance's statement on Usha's religion; 'Unlike Hinduism...'
item.description: Commentator Dinesh D'Souza defended JD Vance's remarks about his wife Usha Vance's religion, stating Christianity is a religion of conversion. Vance expressed a hope for his wife's conversion, sparking controversy and accusations of pandering to the MAGA base, despite their Hindu marriage and son's Indian name. Usha Vance previously stated no intention to convert.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oman Royal Police dismantle major international drug trafficking network
item.description: Oman’s Royal Police have arrested five individuals of Asian nationality linked to an international drug trafficking network. The suspects were intercepted while attempting to smuggle narcotics into the Sultanate, with some drugs intended for domestic distribution and others for re-export. Operations involved coordinated raids across South Al Batinah, reflecting Oman’s ongoing efforts to combat narcotics and maintain public safety
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
